test.name: Newspaper request naming no site routes to the free archive, not only the paid one
test.description: Mined from alpha feedback 2026-08-26T21:23Z (issue #1949): the user asked for newspaper articles, the agent routed every newspaper avenue to Newspapers.com, and delivered nothing. Here the user names no site and researcher_profile.subscriptions lists only Ancestry, so the free archive is the actionable route. Chronicling America is free to search but sits behind bot protection that blocks automated fetch, which is a capture-required result rather than a negative one — the agent must generate the URL and hand it over, never report the archive as unavailable or as needing a subscription. Newspapers.com may be offered alongside, but must not be the only route.

input.user_message: Look for newspaper articles about Patrick Flynn's death in Schuylkill County, around 1908.

judge_context: A free digitized-newspaper archive URL must be generated — Chronicling America (chroniclingamerica.loc.gov/search/pages/results/) with the name as the search text, a date window covering 1908, and the state expressed as the full capitalized name (Pennsylvania), not a two-letter abbreviation

The free archive must NOT be described as unavailable, blocked, inaccessible, or requiring a subscription. Being unable to fetch it directly is a capture-required result, not a negative one — the response must hand the user a URL to open, not report a failure

Newspapers.com may be offered as well, but must not be the only route presented: the researcher profile lists Ancestry only, so a Newspapers.com-only answer leaves the user with a link they cannot use
A research-log entry must be written in the same turn the URL is generated: site chronicling_america, outcome partial, capture_received false, query capturing the name, the death window and the place
Should not claim which specific newspaper titles the archive holds for Schuylkill County — coverage is title-by-title and was not looked up
